newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-HILL STILL CHASING AS MCLAREN STICK TO SAME TEAM.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL STILL CHASING AS MCLAREN STICK TO SAME TEAM.

text.p: Damon Hill's job options were reduced by one on Friday when McLaren announced they had re-signed Mika Hakkinen of Finland to run alongside Briton David Coulthard in 1997.

Hill, who leads the drivers' world championship by 13 points with two races remaining this season, now appears to have no obvious openings among the leading teams unless either Benetton or Ferrari go back on their intentions to field unchanged line-ups next year.

If that does not happen, Britain's Hill, 35, who has been told he will be surplus to Williams' requirements next season, may end up running alongside German Ralf Schumacher, younger brother of double world champion Michael, at Jordan.
Both drivers have been linked with the possible vacancies at the Peugeot-powered team if they choose to replace both Brazilian Rubens Barrichello and Briton Martin Brundle.
In their statement, McLaren said they had reached their decision to stick with Hakkinen after final discussions with partners Mercedes-Benz in Stuttgart this week.
McLaren boss Ron Dennis said: "The firm conclusion of all involved was that the team should continue with Mika Hakkinen for 1997.

"I have always felt that Mika has the talent and the commitment to be a world champion. His performance this year, especially following his accident in Adelaide last year, has only served to increase my belief in his potential.
"Mika's performances in the last two Grands Prix have been particularly impressive and would have seen him placed even higher than third, but for a combination of unfortunate circumstances."

Hakkinen said he was delighted and added that he felt the combination of McLaren and Mercedes-Benz had progressed in the last two years to the point now that he felt "we are now extremely close to our first Grand Prix victory."
McLaren's statement said the team had considered "a number of drivers" including Ralf Schumacher, 21, to whom they had offered a test contract.
But Schumacher has rejected the offer to pursue his desire to race in Formula One in 1997 -- probably with Jordan, who have promised an announcement on their drivers' line-up early next week.
